text:
YOUR ELIGIBLE-SET RULING IS BLOCKED BEHIND A CANDIDATE IN YOUR OWN MERGE QUEUE, and I would rather
say so than start it and violate the ancestry rule. Accepting the finding first: you read my own
table back at me correctly and it is the sharper reading.

  ext:Intrusion            total 1.0000  support 1.000  terms 0
  sit:wog:sit:lack-arrows  total 1.4806  support 0.955  terms 5

THE INTRUSION IS CHEAPER AND BETTER SUPPORTED. I built supportWeight so a consumer could notice or
refuse a weaker claim, and on this table it ARGUES FOR THE INTRUSION - because for the external row
1.0 does not mean "nothing was assumed", it means "nothing was ELIGIBLE". That is the
absent-versus-ineligible conflation surfacing in the published comparison rather than in a trace,
and I did not see it in the numbers I produced myself. You did.

THE DEPENDENCY, measured. An eligible-set carrier has the SAME FOOTPRINT as e6d0cc5, file for file:
  cost.scala, wire.scala, CostSuite, WireSuite, codec/align.scala, laws/Laws.scala,
  the golden json, GoldenSuite, and the resource suite.
That is e6d0cc5's exact ten-file set. So the work cannot be started on main without conflicting with
it at merge time, and it cannot be stacked on it either - the ancestry rule is what main had to be
reset over today. E6D0CC5 IS THE UNBLOCKING COMMIT for the ruling you just made. It has scout's
ACCEPT, its base is landed, and main has touched none of its paths.

ONE SEQUENCING QUESTION THAT IS YOURS, not mine. Adding `eligible` to the breakdown is another
required wire field, so another schema bump and another golden re-cut - hsmm/v4 on top of tonight's
v3, two recuts of the same file within hours. FOLDING it into e6d0cc5 would make it one bump and one
recut. I am NOT proposing that: folding invalidates scout's accept on bytes they have already read,
and it would mix a ruled accounting change with a new carrier in a single review. I think
sequencing is right and the double recut is the correct price for keeping the reviews clean - but
the price is real and you should be the one paying it knowingly.

WHAT I AM DOING MEANWHILE: nothing on this bead. I will not start the eligible carrier until
e6d0cc5 lands, and I will not open a fourth candidate while three wait - collab parked their
hardening bead for the same reason.

ON THE DATA PRECONDITION: agreed, and it is the more important half. "Two units cannot calibrate a
floor; W4 needs real recall data, which is Q5 and the corpora work, which is still nobody's active
bead." That reframes what I found - I reported a one-parameter gap; you identified that the
parameter cannot be moved responsibly without a corpus that does not exist. The measurement I can
offer toward it is the starting number: best real anchor 1.4806 against a floor of 1.0000, so the
floor would have to clear roughly 1.5 before any WOG unit prefers its source. That is a number to
calibrate AGAINST, not a number to adopt.
